How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action: Approval

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 20, 2024  2
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JANUARY 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-2024 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for January 2024.

  D. FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET UPDATE AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, FOR
  THE GENERAL FUND AND MISSION PLAYHOUSE FUND

  This report provides a fiscal year 2023-24 budget update for the City’s general
  fund and Mission Playhouse fund as of December 31, 2023. The budget update
  incorporates the actual revenue received and expenditures that have occurred
  through December 31, 2023, and projects the financial results for the year
  ending June 30, 2024. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. ORDINANCE NO. 703 RENEWING AND APPROVING THE SAN GABRIEL
  POLICE DEPARTMENT’S UPDATED MILITARY EQUIPMENT USE POLICY 707
  AND FINDING THAT THE ANNUAL MILITARY EQUIPMENT REPORT IS IN
  COMPLIANCE WITH GOVERNMENT CODE 7072(A)

  On August 16, 2022, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 684 approving a
  Military Equipment Use Policy pursuant to Assembly Bill 481. In accordance with

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 20, 2024  3
   the legislation and the Policy, a military equipment report must be submitted
  to the City Council annually for each type of military equipment approved
  within one year of approval, and annually thereafter for as long as the military
  equipment is available for use. Adoption of this ordinance would renew and
  update Lexipol policy 707, approve the annual Military Equipment List as
  required by Government Code 7072(a) and establish a new adoption process
  for any future changes to the military equipment list. No funding has been used
  to acquire any new military equipment defined by Government Code 7070.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Review and approve the Assembly Bill 481 annual report and the updated
  Lexipol Policy 707;
  2. By majority vote introduce and conduct the first reading by title only of
  Ordinance No. 703, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San
  Gabriel, California, Readopting Police Department Lexipol Policy, Section
  707, Military Equipment, pursuant to Assembly Bill (AB) 481 Military
  Equipment Acquisition, Use, and Reporting and Establishing Annual Review
  Process”;
  3. Waive future reading, and schedule the second reading and adoption for
  the next regular Council meeting.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL
  CODE RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW THAT WOULD ALLOW MEDICINAL
  CANNABIS DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 ZONE (ZTA23-004)

  The California Legislature adopted Senate Bill 1186 (SB 1186) in 2022, entitled
  the Medicinal Cannabis Patient’s Right of Access Act, which precludes cities and
  counties from adopting or enforcing regulations that prohibit or have the effect
  of prohibiting the retail sale of medicinal cannabis by delivery. SB 1186 took
  effect on January 1, 2024. This item was continued from the February 6, 2024,
  City Council meeting to allow staff additional time to address the comments
  provided at the meeting. The Fiscal Year 2023-24 Adopted Budget includes the
  cost for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and
  codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 20, 2024  4
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The City reviewed
  the environmental impacts of the proposed ordinance pursuant to the California
  Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code Subsection 21000, et seq.
  “CEQA”) and the CEQA Guidelines. CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) provides
  that a project is exempt from CEQA if the activity is covered by the commonsense
  exemption that CEQA only applies to projects which have the potential for
  causing a significant effect on the environment. The proposed ordinance qualifies
  for this CEQA exemption as there is no possibility that the ordinance will have a
  significant effect on the environment as it amends the City’s Municipal Code to
  impose operating requirements on delivery-only medicinal cannabis retailers,
  which does not affect the environment. Accordingly, the ordinance is not subject
  to further environmental review.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 702;

  2. Waive full reading and adopt Ordinance No. 702 by title only: and

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO MEDICINAL CANNABIS
  DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 (LIGHT MANUFACTURING)
  ZONE, SUBJECT TO A CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

  Alternative Options for Consideration:

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications, or deny
  proposed zone text amendment. If the City Council determines that the proposed
  ordinance or any part of the ordinance should be denied, the appropriate motion
  should be adopted.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 20, 2024  5
   A. PRESENTATION OF THE ALL ARE WELCOME PROGRAM AND ADOPTION
  OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-05 FOR A BUDGET INCREASE OF $1,500

  The City Council approved the Human Equity, Access, and Relations (HEAR)
  Commission’s 2023 Annual Workplan at the April 18, 2023, City Council
  meeting. Included in the workplan was the development of a safe zone/space
  campaign geared toward identifying offices, businesses, and public areas as
  safe spaces for minority populations, specifically the LGBTQ+ population. At the
  June 27, 2023, HEAR Commission meeting the Commission approved the All
  Are Welcome program for submission to the City Council for approval. Current
  staffing levels will be used to develop and implement the All Are Welcome
  program. The cost of marketing/information materials, program supplies and
  development of the educational video is estimated to be $1,500. Should City
  Council approve the program, additional funds would need to be allocated
  from the General Fund to the Community Services Recreation Special
  Departmental account, 121-850-10-21-000 in the amount of $1,500.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the All Are Welcome program
  by adoption of Resolution No. 24-05 and direct staff to begin implementing
  the program.

  Alternatives to Staff Recommendations:

  Should the City Council not wish to approve the staff recommendation, the
  following options are available.

  1. Send the item back to the HEAR Commission with requested amendments
  to the program.

  2. Request that staff work with the HEAR Commission to develop a different
  program in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

  3. Other options that the City Council determines after discussing the item.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 20, 2024  6
   10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, March 5, 2024 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be

MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 20, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:31 P.M. on Tuesday, February 20, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Menchaca.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public
  Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Community Development
  Director Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief Edward Elizalde,
  and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION.
  INITIATION OF LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9
  [C]: ONE CASE

  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz announced that the City Counci l had
  unanimously authorized the City to move forward with the filing of a complaint.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Ch ief City Clerk Clark announced that staff had requested the removal of Item 4E from
  the agenda, to be considered at a future meeting.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Ding to approve the agenda order with the removal of Item 4E.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  February 20, 2024
   Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  2. PRESENTATIONS - None.

I
  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Andrew, resident, commented on the Lunar Lantern Festival and requested translation
  into English in the future, and commented on the start of early voting for the March
  5, 2024, primary election.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Wu, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4D as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

I  The City Council approved the Minutes of the City Council Regular Meetings of
  February 6, 2024.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved January 26, 2024, January 30, 2024, and February 2,
  2024, Registers of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - JANUARY 2024

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for January
  2024.

  D. FISCAL VEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET UPDATE AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, FOR
  THE GENERAL FUND AND MISSION PLAYHOUSE FUND

  The City Council received and filed the report.

I  E. ORDINANCE NO. 703 RENEWING AND APPROVING THE SAN GABRIEL
  POLICE DEPARTMENT'S UPDATED MILITARY EQUIPMENT USE POLICY 707
  AND FINDING THAT THE ANNUAL MILITARY EQUIPMENT REPORT IS IN
  COMPLIANCE WITH GOVERNMENT CODE 7072(A)

  This item was pulled from the agenda; no action was taken.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING M INUTES  Page 2 of 5  February 20, 2024
   A. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW THAT WOULD ALLOW MEDICINAL
  CANNABIS DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 ZONE (ZTA23-004)

  Mayor Harrington opened the continued public hearing.

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart made the staff presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included proposed fees to be included when the Master Fee

I  Schedule is considered and fees to be charged in the meantime; there are no
  pending applications; sales tax considerations; clarification on existing code versus
  proposed new code sections; expired applications require a new application; and
  the ability of the City Council to set minimum standards by resolution.

  There was no public comment; therefore, Mayor Harrington closed the public
  hearing.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Ding, to:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 702 by title only: and

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE) OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO MEDICINAL CANNABIS
  DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 (LIGHT MANUFACTURING) ZONE,
  SUBJECT TO A CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT

I  2. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading and
  adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting. The
  Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PRESENTATION OF THE ALL ARE WELCOME PROGRAM AND ADOPTION OF
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-05 FOR A BUDGET INCREASE OF $1,500

I
  Community Services Manager Matthew Morales-Stephens made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included policy for employees to put personal symbols in their
  work space; no neighboring cities of San Gabriel's size have this program, but
  support the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer or questioning (LGBTQ)
  community in other ways; why this program is narrow and not inclusive of other
  groups; the Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission proposed this
  program based on survey results; the requested budget amendment seeks an
  increase to the Community Services line item for programs; initial and upkeep costs
  for the program; and a one-year review period for the program.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  February 20, 2024
   HEAR Commission Chairperson Chasity Jennings-Nunez, M.D., provided comments
  in favor of the program and adoption of the resolution.
  Andrew, resident, questioned who will approve the program's video presentation
  and suggested additional content for the video related to the safety of business
  owners.

  Discussion included potential backlash on businesses; whether the San Gabriel
  Mission been involved in the logo choice; possible website in support of stop the
  hate for other groups as well; preference to provide resources rather than this

I  program; an All Our Welcome program should include other minority groups;
  referring it back to the HEAR Commission; personal preference of the business
  owner; hotel endorsement; and for the City to endorse it, should be more inclusive
  for all people.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to send the item back to the HEAR
  Commission to craft a broader program as to inclusion.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Omar Gallegos, Vice-Principle of West California Academy of Art and Design,
  expressed concerns about student safety in relation to a growing homeless
  encampment, property damage, syringes, and trash, proposed creating a gate instead
  of a chain link fence, and provided photographs.

  City Manager Lazzaretto responded that the Police Department would look into the
  concerns and that the City's social services provider had visited the area to offer
  options.

I  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto gave a shout out to all staff who made the Lunar Lantern
  Festival so successful.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Wu expressed appreciation to his Council colleagues and staff for a very
  successful Lunar Lantern Festival; reported his attendance at a Soroptimist event;
  commented on a recent accident involving a pedestrian and parking issues due to
  street vending; and stated the urgent need for parking enforcement to curb illegal
  crossing and parking violations for community safety.

  Council Member Menchaca thanked Vice Mayor Wu and Council Member Ding for
  providing an amazing Lunar Lantern Festival and gave details of the event; invited all
  to a Kiwanis event to tour the Mission Playhouse on February 22, 2024, at 11 :30 A.M.;
  and, announced Police Department events: Talk of the Town with Police Chief Elizalde
  on February 24, 2024, from 9:00 A.M. - 10:00 A.M. at the Sheraton, Community

I  Academy coming up in March 2024, and Blood Drive on February 28, 2024.

  Council Member Ding thanked the Community Services, Police, Fire, and Public Works
  Departments, and the City's Public Information Officer for the Lunar Lantern Festival
  and shared his observations about the event; reported his attendance at the Sheraton
  Chinese Lunar New Year event with Vice Mayor Wu, announced he had been honored
  by Supervisory Hilda Solis for helping the Asian Pacific Islander (API) community,
  encouraged the community to vote in the March 5, 2024, primary election; and wished
  all a Happy New Year.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  February 20, 2024
   Council Member Chan reported his attendance at the San Gabriel Chamber of
  Commerce's Tasty Tuesday at Luna's Restaurant, commended staff for a great Lunar
  New Year Lantern Festival, and commented on improvements that could be made for
  future events.

  Mayor Harrington stated the Lantern event was excellent, expressed appreciation for
  staff's work on the event, commented that parking is an issue for all venues, and made
  a suggestion for a shuttle van or SG Ride for those not able to make the walk as easily.

I  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 7:53 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:

  Approved this 5th day of March, 2024:
